knowledge_type_note: Official rule. Underpromotion is a consequence of the rule, not a separate rule.
definition_short: A pawn reaching the far rank is replaced, as part of the same move, by a queen, rook, bishop or knight of the same colour.
definition_long:
A pawn reaching the eighth rank (first rank for Black) must be exchanged, as part of the same move, for a new queen, rook, bishop or knight of the same colour. The choice is not restricted to pieces already captured, and there is no limit on how many of a kind may be on the board.

FIDE Art. 4.6 governs the physical act: 'the pawn does not have to be placed on the square of arrival', the order of removing pawn and placing piece does not matter, and 'if an opponent's piece stands on the square of promotion, it must be captured.' Art. 4.4.4: the choice is finalised when the new piece touches the promotion square.

Choosing something other than a queen is UNDERPROMOTION, and is correct when a queen would stalemate, or when a knight's move is what the position needs (a check or fork a queen cannot give).

preconditions: A pawn is moving to the eighth rank (White) or first rank (Black)

exceptions: Promotion is compulsory: a pawn may not remain a pawn.
Underpromotion to a rook avoids stalemate where a queen would cause it; underpromotion to a knight gains a check or fork unavailable to a queen.
limitations: TYPICAL_CONFIDENCE RAISED medium -> high, 2026-09-02, and the reason is the schema's own definition of the field: 'how confidently this concept can normally be asserted ONCE ITS PRECONDITIONS HOLD'. This concept's recognition is MECHANICAL and its knowledge type already carries a high ceiling, so once the preconditions hold there is nothing left to be uncertain about - a stalemate is a stalemate, and a fork this base reports is one findMotifs() found, which ARCHITECTURE.md makes the authority and forbids second-guessing. 'Medium' was the default across 32 rule and motif records regardless of detectability, and it was found by measuring what the API reports against what each record permits: twelve concepts were reporting ABOVE their own record. The fix was to make each record its own ceiling in cap(), which then required the records that were wrong to be corrected rather than silently overruled.

This is a DEFINITIONAL example: the feature is present by the rules of chess and by the page's own move generator, which is the whole of what needs verifying. No engine was consulted, because no engine is needed to establish that a legal move exists. Provenance: the puzzle corpus is engine self-play — a real position from a real game between engines, not a master game.

by_level.beginner: A pawn reaching the far end of the board turns into another piece — almost always a queen.
by_level.intermediate: Promotion. A queen is right nearly always, but check for stalemate, and check whether a knight would give a decisive check or fork.
by_level.advanced: Art. 3.7.5 / 4.6. Underpromotion is justified by stalemate avoidance or by knight geometry.
